title: Damascus Falls, Israel Is Stripped
overview: Isaiah announces the ruin of Damascus and its ally, the northern kingdom of Israel, leaving only a few survivors who turn back to God, and ends with roaring enemy nations suddenly scattered.

parts.label: Damascus and its ally fall (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: Damascus was the capital of Aram (Syria), which had teamed up with the northern kingdom of Israel, here called Ephraim, to attack Judah. Assyria crushed Damascus around 732 BC, and the point is that both allies would share the same ruin.

parts.label: Israel's harvest stripped bare (vv. 4-6)
parts.note: Israel's pride, its people and wealth, wastes away like a body losing weight and is cut down like grain in the rich Valley of Rephaim near Jerusalem. Only a few survivors remain, like the handful of olives left on the top branches after a tree is beaten.

parts.label: Turning from homemade gods (vv. 7-8)
parts.note: The survivors will look to the God of Israel instead of altars and objects they made with their own hands. Asherah poles were wooden poles honoring a goddess, and the other objects were incense altars or possibly sun images, since the exact word is uncertain.

parts.label: Forgotten God, failed gardens (vv. 9-11)
parts.note: Strong cities become overgrown ruins, perhaps like the old towns abandoned when Israel first entered the land, though the Hebrew of verse 9 is hard to read. The people planted fine gardens with imported vines, possibly for a fertility ritual, but because they forgot God their 'Rock,' the harvest ends in grief.

parts.label: Roaring nations scattered (vv. 12-14)
parts.note: Hostile nations roar like a stormy sea, yet when God rebukes them they blow away like chaff from a hilltop threshing floor. Many readers link this to the Assyrian army that besieged Jerusalem and was suddenly gone overnight (Isaiah 37), though the passage names no one.

disagreement: Most Christians read the fall of Damascus as fulfilled when Assyria destroyed it in the 700s BC, while some see verse 1 as a prophecy still waiting for a future, final destruction of the city.
think: When something you relied on for security gives way, what does that tend to reveal about where you had been placing your trust?
